look_here_first: Start with woolly gray stems/leaves AND side of unopened head. C. ochrocentrum has strong, often straw-yellow phyllary spines (FNA large-headed keyed forms ~5–12 mm, other forms longer), while several middle/upper leaves may extend onto the stem as SPINY WINGS up to ~5 cm. Check glutinous/resinous midribs on outer/middle phyllaries if visible. The gray wool and yellowish spines ALONE do not distinguish it from C. undulatum or other western thistles.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Woolly gray tomentum across stems and lower leaf surfaces, in conjunction with other characters.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Long stout phyllary-spine tips, often ~5–12 mm in FNA large-headed form; measure from bract tip, not flower.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Mid and distal stem leaves can be DECURRENT as spiny wings, about 1–5 cm in keyed large-headed form.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Outer/middle phyllaries often with a translucent or sticky resinous median ridge; inspect macro.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: C. undulatum also gray-woolly; it has different leaf lobe form, less uniformly pronounced stem wings, and unusually large mature 6–7 mm cypselae.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Native status in Texas broadly does not prove target-zone counties; current Kerr-only provisional range retained.
